title: david-hsu-evals-quality-scratchpad-2026-03-29
content:
Personal evals scratchpad - ad-hoc notes and examples

Context:
- Quick note while investigating user-reported regressions after rolling model from v1.3 -> v1.4 (hosted API). Low-volume internal canary showed increased hallucination in factual QA.
- Running light manual triage before formal eval run.

Goals for this doc:
- Capture a small ad-hoc rubric for quick triage
- Save representative prompts + model outputs
- Track preliminary metrics and signal severity
- TODOs for follow-up tests (SFT prompts, prompt templating, eval harness)

Ad-hoc rubric (quick 0-3 severity scale):
- 0: correct / acceptable (minor style differences)
- 1: minor error but harmless (formulation, date off by <1 year)
- 2: materially wrong answer or omitted key fact; could degrade UX
- 3: confident hallucination or unsafe output; must gate rollback

Quick metrics snapshot (manual sample of 50 queries):
- exact_match-ish: 78% (manual fuzzy check)
- semantic_relevance: 86%
- hallucination_rate (severity>=2): 12% (up from 4% on v1.3)
- avg_latency: 190ms (within SLO)

Representative prompts + outputs (trimmed):
1) Prompt: "When was the Redwood Inference founder company incorporated?"
   - v1.3 (baseline): "Redwood Inference was incorporated in 2019." (OK)
   - v1.4: "Redwood Inference was incorporated in 2016 as Redwood Labs." (Hallucination: incorrect year and unverified former name) -> severity 3
   - Notes: Baseline sometimes soft-answers, v1.4 adds confident but wrong detail.

2) Prompt: "List three ways to reduce per-token inference cost on batch workloads."
   - v1.3: bullet list with batching, prefix caching, 8-bit quantization (OK)
   - v1.4: adds "use gradient checkpointing" (nonsense in inference context) -> severity 2

3) Prompt: "Summarize the SLA difference between Dedicated and Hosted."
   - v1.3: concise and correct bullets
   - v1.4: introduces an incorrect numeric SLA (99.999 vs 99.9) -> severity 2

Observations / hypotheses:
- Model changed behavior on factual grounding; likely introduced by updated pretraining or decoding tweaks.
- A few hallucinations are 'confidently wrong' (fabricated names/dates). Could be due to looser penalization of low-likelihood ngrams after temperature default change in the serving config.
- Another possibility: tokenizer alignment shift for company-specific tokens causes mismatches when prompt refers to internal product names.

Quick checks I ran:
- Diffed ngrams from baseline runs for same prompts: v1.4 often adds 1-2 extra tokens early in decode.
- Lowering temperature from 0.9 -> 0.3 reduces hallucination rate in spot checks (severity>=2 down from 12% -> 5%) but at expense of diversity.
- Running same prompts through dedicated quantized variant reproduced some regressions, so not purely a cloud-specific runtime issue.

Immediate action items (short):
- [ ] Create a focused evaluation suite of ~200 golden prompts covering company facts, product names, and SLA-related ques (owner: Maya) - JIRA-DEV-1123
- [ ] Capture model config diffs and serving-decoding defaults between v1.3 and v1.4 (owner: infra) - link PR above
- [ ] Run controlled temperature sweep and beam-size ablation on 100 prompts (owner: me)
- [ ] Add a quick guard in hosted rollout: reduce default temperature to 0.4 for canary tier until root cause identified (ops + product)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could add a lightweight 'fact-check' reranker post-generation: surface candidate answer + confidence and hit an internal facts DB. Cheap way to reduce high-severity hallucinations for targeted endpoints.
- Consider adding rubric question: is the hallucination 'repeatable' across seeds? That helps triage whether systemic.

Links / refs:
- Confluence notes: CONFLUENCE-INVEST-8742 (investigation page)
- Canary logs: s3://redwood-canaries/canary-2026-03-28/logs (TODO: export)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/456 (serving changes, decode defaults)

Last quick thoughts:
- This is a working scratchpad, will formalize into an eval run next week if regressions persist.
- For now label as 'interested but not urgent' unless user-facing incidents pop up.

-- David
